name: Primes on Interval
trail: Sieve up to b, then prefix count pre[i] = primes in [1, i], so any window [x, x + l - 1] has pre[x + l - 1] - pre[x - 1] primes in O(1).
check(l) slides x over a..b - l + 1: O(b - a).
Monotone: any (l + 1)-window contains the l-window at the same x, so check over l is 0 0 0 1 1 1. Binary search the first 1 in [1, b - a + 1].
-1 exactly when even the full range [a, b] has fewer than k primes (b - a + 1 < k is only one such case: 1 4 3 has length 4 but 2 primes). No 1 in the 0-1 array, so ans stays -1.
Total O(b log log b + (b - a) log(b - a)), about 2e7 for b = 1e6.

name: Sum in the tree
trail: Known s_v and s_p give a_v = s_v - s_p, which must be >= 0.
Erased (even-depth) v: for each child c, a_v + a_c = s_c - s_p is fixed. Raising a_v by 1 lowers every child by 1, so the total changes by 1 - (#children) <= 0. Push a_v as high as allowed.
a_c >= 0 for all children caps it: a_v = min over children of (s_c - s_p), i.e. s_v = min child s. No children: a_v = 0, s_v = s_p.
Answer -1 if any a_v < 0 (some s_v < s_p).
dfs1 gets depth, dfs2 fills s at even depth, a loop sums a_i = s_i - s_par. O(n). Sum up to 1e5 * 1e9, long long.

name: The Two Routes
trail: Question: minimize max(train arrival, bus arrival) at n, never in the same town (except n) at the same time.
Simplify: drop the meeting rule -> each vehicle alone is a BFS (unit edges), answer max of the two.
Fact: every pair has exactly one of railway / road. So the pair (1, n) is one of them: one vehicle reaches n at time 1.
Proof the rule never breaks: the fast one is at n from time 1 on, and n is allowed. (Two BFS paths in general CAN meet: U-V rail, K-V road.)
Answer = BFS on both graphs, max of the two; -1 if either can't reach n.
Road graph is the complement, up to n^2 edges: O(n^2) for n = 400.

name: Love Rescue
trail: Question: buy the fewest letter pairs (c1, c2), each usable any number of times both ways on both strings, so the strings can be made equal.
Small cases: (ab, da) -> 2, (ax, yz) -> 2, (ab, ba) -> 1. Position i gives the letter pair (s_i, t_i).
Graph on 26 letters, edges = bought spells. Done iff for every i, s_i and t_i are in the same component (NOT "one component overall").
Optimal has no cycle: dropping a cycle edge keeps components the same. So a component of k letters costs exactly k - 1 spells.
Union-find over the n pairs; each union that joins two groups is a spell to print. O(n) on 26 letters.

name: Bear and Two Paths
trail: Question: build two paths through all n cities, a...b and c...d, no road a-b or c-d, at most k distinct roads total; else -1.
Fact: distinct = 2n - 2 - shared, so maximize shared roads.
n = 4 is impossible: the a...b path's middle is {c, d}, forcing c-d.
Construction: a c x1..xm d b and c a x1..xm b d (m = n - 4). Shared: a-c, b-d and the m - 1 middle roads -> n + 1 distinct roads.
Proof n + 1 is the minimum: in path 1, a and b are endpoints (1 road each); in path 2 they are inside (2 roads each). With only n roads the single extra road must touch both, i.e. be a-b: forbidden.
Answer -1 if n == 4 or k < n + 1, else print the two paths. O(n).

name: Mike and Shortcuts
trail: Question: for every i, the cheapest walk from 1 to i, where a step U -> V costs |U - V|, except the shortcut U -> a_U costs 1.
Simplify: a walk U -> V that never turns back costs the same as stepping one intersection at a time through every node in between.
So the n^2 walking edges shrink to i -> i + 1 and i -> i - 1 (both directions!), cost 1 each. Add the shortcuts i -> a_i, cost 1. About 3n edges.
Every edge costs 1, so a walk's energy = its number of edges, so the fewest edges from 1 (plain BFS from the single source 1) = min energy.
Trap: "always take the shortcut" is false (a_1 = 5, target 2: shortcut costs 4, walking costs 1). BFS picks the edges, not you.

name: Igor and his way to work
trail: Question: is there an S -> T path that avoids * and has at most 2 turns?
Look at the optimal: any such path is at most 3 straight segments (straight, L, C or Z).
Trap: printing the BFS path, as in Monsters, checks one path, the shortest, which can turn too often. The question asks about any path.

Encode the turn into the node: node = enc(i, j, d) = (i*m + j)*4 + d, 4nm states. The edge to the next cell in direction e costs 0 if e == d (straight), else 1 (a turn). nei(u) builds the edges on the fly, because a stored g (1.6e7 edges) would blow 256 MB.
Start at S in all 4 directions at cost 0. YES iff the minimum cost over T's 4 directions is <= 2.
Proof: a path's cost is exactly its number of turns, so min cost <= 2 iff some path has <= 2 turns.
0-1 BFS template (cost-0 edges to the front of the deque, cost-1 edges to the back): O(nm), about 1.6e7 steps.

name: Gas Station
trail: Start i valid iff tank = sum of g[k] - c[k] over k = (i + t) % n, t = 0..n-1, never goes below 0. Brute force: test every i, O(n^2).
Let T be the first step where the walk from i goes negative. For j = (i + s) % n, 0 < s <= T, split the sum at s: A + B < 0 with A >= 0 (s - 1 < T), so B < -A <= 0 and j fails too.
So every start i..i + T is ruled out; next try i + T + 1. test(i) returns T, or n if i never fails.
Loop while i < n: starts 0..i - 1 are already ruled out, and a walk that wraps (i + T + 1 >= n) rules out the rest, so return -1.
O(n): failed walks cover disjoint stations (at most n total), plus one successful walk of n.
